findings.problem: QuoteWorkflow has no explicit state machine; valid transitions cannot be enforced at the type level. Any method can be called in any order, allowing invalid state combinations.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set status to any string, clear is_sent, or construct QuoteWorkflow with is_validated=true and status=anything, creating logically impossible states that only runtime checks could catch.
findings.fix: Replace QuoteWorkflow with a Rust enum `QuoteStatus` representing discrete states (Draft, Validated, Sent, Cancelled) and use a state-machine type that makes illegal transitions untypeable.

findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value. mark_sent at line 10 assigns "sent".to_string() but any code can assign invalid values like "deleted", "", or null-equivalents.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set item.status = "deleted" or item.status = "" which the rest of the system would treat as a legitimate status, causing incorrect branching, logging, or database writes with unparseable status values.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: QuoteStatus` where QuoteStatus is an enum with explicitly named variants. Remove all String-based status assignment.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are lifecycle booleans that create combinatorial explosion of invalid state combinations (validated without status, sent without validated, etc.).
findings.failure_mode: A QuoteWorkflow can exist with is_validated=false and is_sent=true, meaning the quote was sent before being validated. These booleans are independently mutable so any transition order is type-allowed.
findings.fix: Collapse lifecycle booleans into a single QuoteStatus enum with variants that encode the workflow position, e.g. `enum QuoteStatus { Draft, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Each variant owns only the data it needs.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate field from is_sent, creating two independent sources of truth. Option is None while is_sent is true is a valid but impossible state.
findings.failure_mode: Code checking is_sent=true will expect sent_at_epoch_ms to be Some, but it could be None if someone set is_sent without setting sent_at_epoch_ms, leading to None.unwrap() panics or silent data loss.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of a QuoteStatus enum so only the Sent variant carries the timestamp. Option is no longer needed; the variant discriminant carries the truth.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. Any string is accepted as a valid quote ID, including empty strings, UUIDs, SQL fragments, or other values that should be rejected.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can pass id="" or id="SELECT * FROM quotes" which would be treated as a valid quote ID. No validation, length checks, or format constraints are enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace `pub id: String` with `pub id: QuoteId` where QuoteId is a newtype wrapping a validated string or uuid::Uuid, with a smart constructor that rejects empty/malformed IDs and returns a typed error.

findings.problem: raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly. QuoteWorkflow accepts String for id, status and Option<u64> for sent_at_epoch_ms without any validation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can do QuoteWorkflow { id: "".to_string(), status: "bogus".to_string(), is_validated: true, .. } producing a struct that violates every domain invariant. No parse boundary exists to enforce validity.
findings.fix: Replace the struct with a QuoteStatus enum + QuoteId newtype. Provide fallible smart constructors (e.g. QuoteId::new(s: &str) -> Result<QuoteId, ParseError>) at all entry points. The domain core should only ever receive validated values.
